Matching contract (the guard reads `toolInput.command`; a missing or non-string command is denied):
1. Split the command into segments on unquoted `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newline. Allow only when every segment is an allowed form. Matching is anchored and whole-command, like `ConductorGuard.RunStartCommand`; never a substring match. Unparseable input is denied.
2. Denied anywhere: `$(...)`, backticks, `$` outside single quotes (double quotes included), `<(` and `>(`, unquoted `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, a heredoc `<<`, a background `&`, any redirect except `2>&1` and (Bash only) `2>/dev/null`, a leading `NAME=value` assignment, the shell keywords `for`, `while`, `until`, `if`, `then`, `do`, `done`, `case`, `function`, `select`, unbalanced quotes, an empty segment, and in Bash an unquoted backslash.
3. Wrapper commands are never allowed forms: `bash`, `sh`, `zsh`, `pwsh`, `powershell`, `eval`, `exec`, `xargs`, `env`, `command`, `sudo`, `nohup`, `time`, `source`, `.`.
4. PowerShell uses the same tokenizer and forms; a backtick and `$` (so `$()`, `@()` and variables) are denied, `&` as a call operator is denied, and a backslash is literal so Windows paths work.
5. Allowed forms:
   - `kyber-weave docs validate <dir> --merge-ready`, `kyber-weave docs drift <dir>`, `kyber-weave doctor --ensure` (a path operand may replace `.`); `codegraph explore "..."`.
   - `git [--no-pager] [-C <dir>] (log|diff|status|show|rev-parse) [args]`. Denied: any other global option (so `-c`, `--config-env`, `--exec-path`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--namespace`), `--output` or `--output=...` on any subcommand, and every other subcommand (`checkout`, `commit`, `fetch`, `grep`, `ls-files`, `blame`, and so on).
   - `grep`; `rg` with `--pre`, `--pre-glob`, `-z` and `--search-zip` denied; `ls`; `find` with `-exec`, `-execdir`, `-ok`, `-okdir`, `-delete`, `-fprint`, `-fprint0`, `-fprintf` and `-fls` denied; and as standalone readers or pipe filters `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `cut`, `sort` (with `-o`, `--output` and `--compress-program` denied) and `uniq` (at most one file operand).
   - `cd <dir>` with exactly one operand (no flags, not `-`), followed by `&&` (or `;` in PowerShell). Track the effective directory across `cd` segments.
   - `touch` with no flags, one or more literal operands and no glob characters (`*?[{`). Resolve each operand against the effective directory (the payload `cwd`, then any `cd`) and normalise it. It must contain no `..` after normalisation, its absolute path must contain `/<dir>/` for one of the planning directories passed in, and the file name must end in `.md` or `.json`.
6. Everything else is denied, with the replacement named in the reason: `cat`, `sed`, `awk` (use the Read tool, with offset and limit); `git grep`, `git ls-files`, `git blame` (use CodeGraph, `grep` or `find`); `git fetch` (the conductor fetches); `gh`, `curl`, `wget` (network; ask the conductor to relay); `python`, `node` and any interpreter (no scripts); `echo`, `printf`, `pwd`, `tee`.

Background. The architect agent's shell boundary was instruction-only (`architect.md` says "The lattice cannot enforce this list; you keep it."). A parallel task adds a stateless Arbiter hook guard, `ArchitectShellGuard` (`src/KyberWeave.Arbiter/Hooks/ArchitectShellGuard.cs`), permanent id `KW-ARB-SHELL-001`, beside `ReadGuard` and `ConductorGuard`. On Claude it denies any architect `Bash` or `PowerShell` call outside the documented list before it runs. It is rendered by `ClaudeRenderer.BuildArbiterHooks` as a `PreToolUse` entry with matcher `^(Bash|PowerShell)$` in the architect's agent file at Project scope and at Global (user) scope. A test, `KyberWeave.Tests.Arbiter.ArchitectShellGuardSyncTests`, binds the backticked spans of the architect command-set clause to the guard's `DocumentedForms` keys.

Decisions to record (they are final):
- Guard, not rule. Rejected: a shipped rule in `default-rules.yml`. The rule engine evaluates dispatch triggers only; every decision becomes a ledger event and repeat counts stop tasks (ADR 0070); shell calls are frequent and have no claim key, so a global and a project hook could both record one call; a rule would need a new trigger family, would change the shipped-rule count and its pinning tests, and would let hosts tune or disable a security boundary by id. Hook guards are not rules: hosts cannot tune or disable them, and they write no ledger event.
- Matching: whole-command, anchored, allow-by-form and deny-on-unparseable. Commands split on unquoted `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, newline; substitution, backticks, `$`, process substitution, subshells, braces, heredocs, background `&`, redirects other than `2>&1` and `2>/dev/null`, env-prefix assignments, shell keywords (loops, conditionals), wrapper commands (`bash`, `sh`, `eval`, `xargs`, `env`, `sudo`, and so on), `git -c` and other git global options except `--no-pager` and `-C`, `git ... --output`, `find -exec/-ok/-delete`, `rg --pre`, `sort -o` are all denied. `touch` is allowed only for `.md` or `.json` files under the plan, spec and todo directories.
- User scope: Claude Code runs frontmatter hooks of user-level sub-agents (`~/.claude/agents/`) without the trust step while that sub-agent is active, and a project sub-agent of the same name outranks the user one, so exactly one file's hooks fire. Rendering the shell matcher into the user-level agent file is an exception to Req 22.2 (nothing is rendered per agent at Global scope). Rejected: a `^(Bash|PowerShell)$` matcher in user-level `settings.json`, which would start the hook process for every shell call of every agent on the machine and fire twice beside a project agent-file hook. At Global scope the event is evaluated under the project config when the project enables Arbiter, under the user config when there is none, and passed when the project sets `arbiter.enabled: false`.
- Harness matrix: enforced on Claude only (`Bash` and `PowerShell` tools, project and user scope). Copilot VS Code (terminal tool name in the payload undocumented), Copilot CLI (gates only `task`), Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo, Pi, Factory, Devin and Antigravity (dispatch-only adapters) are follow-ups; there the list stays instruction-only.
- Enforced at once, no shadow mode, no configuration, like `ReadGuard` and `ConductorGuard`. A wrongly denied command costs one BLOCKED round trip.
- Finding for the runbook: the worker read guard does not cover the `PowerShell` tool (`ClaudeHookAdapter.IsReadTool` and `ClaudeRenderer.ReadGuardMatcher` name `Bash` only); a follow-up.
